title: Accelerator replacement acceptance and degraded-mode playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This document is a runbook draft for validating accelerator (GPU/TPU/A100/NVLink) replacements and for orchestrating a controlled degraded-mode for inference clusters while hardware is replaced or capacity is being added. It is meant for SREs on-call and platform engineers doing physical swaps, node reimaging or rolling maintenance where we must preserve customer SLAs by graceful degradation and fast acceptance testing.

Scope:
- Applies to inference fleets hosting Redwood Dedicated and Private nodes and to ephemeral pools backing hosted API.
- Covers: cordon/drain, device replacement validation, kernel/driver checks, volume remount validation, warmup/kv-cache priming, capacity rebalancing, and degraded-mode routing.

Non-goals:
- Deep vendor-specific hardware repair procedure (follow OEM manual).
- Long-term performance tuning (see Optimize team docs).

Quick decision matrix (oncall):
- Severity P0 (total capacity < 10% of expected or > 3 availability zones impacted): escalate to SRE lead and ENG infra manager immediately.
- Severity P1 (noticeable tail latency increase > 30% or error rate > 3% sustained 5m): start degraded-mode and follow acceptance checklist.
- If capacity shortfall is short-lived (< 30 min) and autoscale can absorb, monitor and defer manual replacement unless hardware is marked DOA.

Channels and paging:
- Primary incident channel: #sre-infra (Slack)
- Secondary escalation: #eng-infra-ops
- Oncall pager: SRE oncall rotation (PagerDuty)

Prereqs before physical swap or planned maintenance:
- Confirm maintenance window with customer impact (if Dedicated/Private).
- Ensure recent golden AMI/container image is available and validated.
- KMS keys and vault access checked (if reimaging).
- Backup critical local state if present (checkpoint KV cache metadata to object store).
- Run capacity forecast (sheet id: CONFLUENCE-1234) and mark required extra nodes.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Oncall SRE: triage, cordon/drain, live validation, rollback decision.
- Hardware Tech (Field): physical GPU replacement, health LED checks, PCI reseat.
- Platform Eng: kernel/driver compatibility, image rebuild if needed.
- Product Ops: customer communication if Dedicated/Private.

Core runbook steps (planned maintenance):
1) Pre-checks (15m before):
   - Query cluster health: kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=inference-pool=true
   - Check model-serving pods: kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Running
   - Validate node GPU nominal: /usr/local/bin/gpu-health-check.sh <node> (returns PASS/FAIL).
   - Record baseline tail latency and 99th: prometheus query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)).

2) Enter maintenance mode & traffic control:
   - Add node to maintenance pool in control plane: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/pools/<pool>/maintenance -d '{"node": "<node>"}'
   - For hosted API: enable routing fallback to replica region via routing policy: /ops/routing/fallback toggle (remember to annotate why).
   - Reduce model concurrency on remaining instances if SLO risk: set concurrency=1 for heavy models via admin API.

3) Cordon + drain (Kubernetes):
   - kubectl cordon <node>
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
   - Verify pods rescheduled: kubectl get pods -n inference --watch (confirm pod counts stable).

4) Hardware replacement steps (field tech):
   - Power down node via BMC, follow electrostatic best practices.
   - Replace accelerator, reseat power cables, verify firmware matches expected revision (FW 58.2.x).
   - Boot node to single-user, run /opt/hw/verify_firmware.sh and nvml-based health scan: python3 /opt/hw/nvml_smoke.py
   - Capture dmesg and lspci output and attach to incident: /var/log/dmesg.txt, /tmp/lspci.txt

5) Rejoin node to cluster (after field tech signals done):
   - Power on and confirm node boots into golden AMI/image.
   - Confirm node registers: kubectl get nodes | grep <node> (should be Ready).
   - Run node-level validation: /usr/local/bin/node-acceptance-checks.sh <node> (checks drivers, nvidia-smi, nv_peer_memory, rdma, kernel modules).

6) Accelerator acceptance tests (automation):
   - Run small synthetic inference workload (100 warmup requests, 300 requests at production qps scaled-down) against node-local endpoint. Verify:
     - p50/p95/p99 within 10% of baseline
     - GPU memory stable (no OOM)
     - No CUDA errors in logs (/var/log/inference-service.log)
   - If fails: mark node OutOfService, escalate to Platform Eng and Hardware vendor.

7) KV cache and model warmup:
   - Prime KV cache for common prefixes using warmup runner: /ops/warmup/prime --models common-model-list --target-node <node>
   - Run eviction/restore sanity: ensure model shards load and shard-local cache hits > 70% within 5m.

8) Rebalance and capacity check:
   - Remove maintenance flag from pool and allow scheduler to rebalance.
   - Run traffic ramp (gradual): traffic-router scale increments: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 15m intervals while monitoring latency and errors.
   - Confirm autoscaler is healthy and not oscillating: kubectl get hpa -n inference --watch

9) Post-acceptance and closeout:
   - Annotate incident channel with links to acceptance logs and perf graphs.
   - Update node tag with hardware serial and firmware version.
   - Close maintenance ticket in JIRA and mark hardware vendor ticket if any.

Unplanned / emergency replacement (short checklist):
- If a node exhibits ECC errors, repeated OOMs or NVML unrecoverables: immediately cordon and drain the node, trigger degraded-mode routing and start replacement with spare node.
- If path to replace will take > 60 minutes, proactively reduce model concurrency, and schedule regional routing fallback.

Degraded-mode behaviors (what to enable):
- Route low-priority customer traffic to lower-cost model variant or CPU fallback pool.
- Enable early-cutoff stream responses for high-latency requests to preserve tail SLOs.
- Toggle model-level circuit breakers: admin API: POST /ops/circuit-breaker/{model}/trip -> reason=maintenance

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- New node shows Ready and passes node-acceptance-checks.sh
- Synthetic workload: p99 < baseline_p99 * 1.15 and error rate < 0.5%
- KV cache warmup hits > 70% on common prefixes within 10 minutes
- No driver/kernel warnings in dmesg for 10m after synthetic run

Rollback conditions:
- If any acceptance test fails or tail latency increases > 50% during traffic ramp, immediately remove node from service and revert routing to previous healthy nodes.
- Record failure artifacts and escalate.

Common commands (cheat-sheet):
- cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- check pods: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide
- node logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
- GPU health: ssh <node> -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv

Notes, open questions and TODOs (working doc):
- TODO: automate acceptance synthetic runner to post to incident channel with graphs. (Priya owns)
- TODO: define SLA delta thresholds for Dedicated customers (Product Ops)
- Question: should we maintain a hot-spare node pool for each AZ or cross-AZ warm spares? Pros/cons TODO (Mark to evaluate cost).
- Draft idea: add a bootstrap job that preloads top-20 prefixes into any new node within the first 2 minutes so first warmup is faster.

Post-incident review template (fill after closure):
- Timeline of actions (UTC): detection, cordon, field swap, acceptance, restore traffic.
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (logs, dmesg, vendor RMA).
- What worked / what failed in the process.
- Action items, owners, and ETA.

Appendix: quick links
- Golden image CI (AMI): https://ci.redwood/golden-images
- Acceptance runner repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acceptance-runner
- Incident board template: CONFLUENCE-1234

This is a living draft — expect changes as we iterate on automation and degraded-mode routing. If you add a test or command here, include reproducible steps and a snippet that others can copy/paste.

Change log (brief):
- 2026-02-10: initial draft by Ana R.
- 2026-02-20: added degraded-mode toggles and traffic ramp guidance (Mark C.)
- 2026-03-10: acceptance criteria tightened; added KV cache warmup steps (Priya K.)
